questions.q: What is the PowerShell console best suited for?
options: Writing and maintaining a 200-line script over several weeks
Editing a script with real syntax highlighting and autocomplete
A quick, one-off interactive command — nothing is saved when you close the window
Debugging a script line by line with breakpoints
questions.explain: The console is a read-eval-print loop: great for a quick answer, but there's no saving, no real editing, and no syntax highlighting.

questions.q: What is a key limitation of the PowerShell ISE?
options: It only exists on Linux and macOS
It cannot run any PowerShell commands at all
It's stuck on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Microsoft no longer actively develops it
It requires a paid Microsoft subscription to open
questions.explain: The ISE was superseded years ago and can't run PowerShell 7+, though you'll still find it preinstalled on older servers.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend VS Code with the PowerShell extension as the real standard?
options: It's what Microsoft actively develops for, with real syntax highlighting, IntelliSense, inline errors, and a debugger
Because VS Code is the only tool that can run a .ps1 file
Because the console and ISE have both been completely removed from Windows
Because it requires no installation and comes preinstalled everywhere
questions.explain: VS Code plus the PowerShell extension gives you tooling none of the older options have, and it's what this course uses from Chapter 3 onward.

questions.q: According to this lesson's honest recommendation, when should you reach for the console instead of VS Code?
options: For every script you write in this entire course
For a one-off command you'll never need again
Only when VS Code is unavailable on the machine
Never — the console should not be used at all
questions.explain: The console is for quick, disposable questions; VS Code is for anything you'll save, rerun, or hand off.

questions.q: Starting in which chapter does this course write every .ps1 script in VS Code?
options: Chapter 1
Chapter 4
This course never writes a .ps1 script
Chapter 3
questions.explain: Chapter 3, "Scripts & Control Flow", is where the course starts writing real .ps1 files, and it does so in VS Code.
